recipe.name: Tim Wendelboe upright light-roast 14 g / 200 g
recipe.grind_description: Fine filter grind for light roast; no universal grinder number

expected_time_s.clock_start: Plunger seated after initial pour and three stirs; steep timer zero
expected_time_s.clock_end: Gentle pressing complete after 60-second sealed steep and second three stirs; press time unspecified

steps.instruction: Rinse a Standard paper filter; fit and lock cap. Stand upright on sturdy mug and add 14 g coffee.
steps.why: Secure support and correct filtration
steps.completion: Flat filter, locked cap and stable setup; rinse discarded

steps.instruction: Tare and pour 200 g freshly boiling water onto coffee.
steps.why: Measured extraction input
steps.completion: Scale shows 200 g added; small initial drip-through allowed

steps.instruction: Stir three times.
steps.why: Wet and mix grounds
steps.completion: Three stirs complete

steps.instruction: Seat the plunger shallowly, about half an inch; lift slightly if needed without unseating. Start the timer and steep 60 seconds.
steps.why: Limit draining while steeping
steps.completion: 60 seconds after sealing

steps.instruction: Carefully remove plunger, stir three times back to front and reinsert.
steps.why: Complete creator's agitation sequence
steps.completion: Three further stirs complete and plunger seated

steps.instruction: Press gently and steadily on stable support; keep hands clear and do not force the puck.
steps.why: Controlled separation through filter
steps.completion: Liquid ends and trapped air passes through; hiss can be faint

steps.instruction: Safely remove hot cap, eject grounds and filter over a bin, rinse and store seal uncompressed.
steps.why: Remove residue and avoid prolonged seal compression
steps.completion: Clean parts stored without compressing seal

Use gentle pressure; stop forcing if setup shifts or resistance feels unsafe

recipe.name: Counter Culture automatic-brewer 63 g / 1,000 g example
equipment: Automatic paper-filter brewer whose manual permits a 1,000 g reservoir-water batch with 63 g coffee
Burr grinder or appropriately ground coffee
recipe.grind_description: Medium-coarse, slightly finer than kosher salt; a texture reference, not a universal dial setting.

expected_time_s.clock_start: Pressing the machine brew switch, if recording elapsed time
expected_time_s.clock_end: Water delivery has ended and basket drainage has finished; obey model completion instructions

recipe.completion_signal: Machine cycle completes and coffee finishes draining into the receiving vessel. Power-off timing is not assumed to equal brew completion.

steps.instruction: With the machine off, check its allowed batch, filter and receiving vessel; complete required first-use flushing and seat the correct paper.
steps.why: Batch and filter compatibility prevent misuse; preparation differs between models.
steps.completion: Clean compatible basket, paper and carafe are ready; rinse water has been discarded.

steps.instruction: Weigh 1,000 g drinking water separately and transfer it from a clean jug to the reservoir without exceeding its maximum.
steps.why: This quantity is reservoir input; it does not promise 1,000 g beverage output.
steps.completion: The measured batch is in the reservoir and within the machine's allowed capacity.

steps.instruction: Grind 63 g medium-coarse, put it in the basket paper and gently level the loose bed without pressing it down.
steps.why: An even bed helps water reach the coffee; grounds need room to swell.
steps.completion: Dose is loaded, with room for swelling and no grounds obstructing the basket rim.

steps.instruction: Seat basket, receiving vessel and required lids; select the model's batch setting if present, then press brew.
steps.why: Correct assembly keeps hot liquid contained and activates any automatic drip stop.
steps.completion: The machine delivers water and coffee drains normally without overflow.

steps.instruction: Let the machine complete its cycle and the basket finish draining; keep the receiving vessel in place until flow ends.
steps.why: Reservoir emptying and delayed power shutdown do not establish the same completion boundary on every model.
steps.completion: Water delivery has ended and no significant coffee flow remains.

steps.instruction: Serve using the vessel handle, then switch off when appropriate; do not heat an empty glass carafe.
steps.why: The beverage and vessel remain hot after the cycle.
steps.completion: Coffee is served safely; actual collected output may be recorded separately.

safety: Use each appliance's manual for minimum/maximum batch and filter compatibility; a generic recipe does not approve every machine.
Keep hands clear of steam and hot outlet arms; use receiving-vessel handles.
On Moccamaster, leave required lids, basket and receiving vessel in place during brewing.
Switch off, unplug and cool before cleaning or clearing an outlet; never immerse the appliance.
Cup-One has no drip stop: keep its mug in place until coffee finishes draining.
Do not continue heating an empty glass carafe; hand-wash Moccamaster glass carafes.
Descaling and cleaner product directions are model-specific; current USA guidance advises against vinegar.

guides.scope: Manual six-cup Classic Chemex with compatible bonded paper; app-authored 30 g coffee and 480 g brew-water starting point. Three-cup and named roaster recipes are separate variants.

recipe.name: Everyday six-cup Chemex: 30 g / 480 g
equipment: Matching bonded paper: FP-1, FC-100, FS-100, or FSU-100
recipe.grind_description: Medium-coarse, visibly granular rather than powder; no universal grinder number.

expected_time_s.clock_start: First brewing water contacts coffee; preparation and rinse excluded
expected_time_s.clock_end: No standing water remains above the bed and continuous flow has become occasional drips

recipe.completion_signal: Water above the grounds has drained; main flow has slowed to occasional drips. Remove the filter without waiting for every last drip.

steps.instruction: Open matching paper with three layers toward the spout and one opposite; leave the spout groove open.
steps.why: Air needs an escape route as brewed coffee enters the carafe.
steps.completion: Paper fits the six-cup funnel and the spout channel remains clear.

steps.instruction: Wet the paper with hot water, discard the rinse, and put the brewer on a stable scale.
steps.why: Our optional preparation warms the glass and wets the paper; rinse is separate from recipe water.
steps.completion: Paper is wet and no rinse water remains in the carafe.

steps.instruction: Add 30 g medium-coarse coffee, level the bed gently, and tare the scale with everything in place.
steps.why: A consistent weighed dose makes this chosen ratio repeatable.
steps.completion: Level coffee bed and scale reads zero before brewing.

steps.instruction: At first water contact start the timer, pour 90 g evenly, gently stir only if needed to wet dry pockets, and wait until 45 seconds elapsed.
steps.why: Wet the whole bed before the main pours. The 90 g and 45 seconds are app-selected, not a Chemex manufacturer recipe.
steps.completion: All grounds wetted and timer reaches 45 seconds from first water contact, including the pour.

steps.instruction: At 45 seconds pour 150 g gently over the coffee to reach 240 g total. Pause whenever liquid rises too quickly.
steps.why: This app-selected checkpoint divides the remaining water into manageable additions.
steps.completion: Scale reads 240 g cumulative; liquid remains comfortably below both rims.

steps.instruction: When the level has visibly fallen, add the final 240 g gradually to reach 480 g total; divide this addition further if needed for headroom.
steps.why: Flow and safe liquid level determine pace; no unsupported fixed pour-start time.
steps.completion: Scale reads 480 g cumulative, without overflow or sealing the spout.

steps.instruction: Observe drainage and record elapsed time when standing water disappears and the continuous flow becomes occasional drips.
steps.why: Completion follows drainage. This untested 30/480 batch has no independently verified finish window.
steps.completion: No standing water above the bed; main flow has become occasional drips.

steps.instruction: Carefully remove the wet filter, gently swirl the collected coffee, and serve using the collar or handle.
steps.why: Mix the collected coffee and protect hands from hot glass.
steps.completion: Filter removed and coffee served safely.

safety: Keep the brewer stable and liquid below both the paper and glass rims; pause pouring if needed.
Handle hot coffee carefully and hold the brewer by collar or handle rather than hot glass.
Let the carafe cool before washing. Remove wood collar and rawhide; handwash with warm soapy water or secure bare glass in the dishwasher.
Do not reheat a Chemex in a microwave.
If cleaning an electric grinder, unplug it and follow its own manual.

guides.scope: Crema Coffee Roasters' 25 g / 400 g water-first recipe in a large Clever with #4 wedge paper; Ozone small-brewer coffee-first recipe is a separate variant.

recipe.name: Crema large-Clever water-first starting recipe
equipment: Stable heat-safe server with capacity for the batch

water_temperature_c.control: user: freshly boiled water poured promptly; boiling temperature depends on local conditions

recipe.grind_description: Finer than ordinary drip coffee, with particle texture described by Crema as wet sand; do not wet dry grounds before brewing.

expected_time_s.clock_start: Coffee enters the already-filled brewer; initial stirring is included
expected_time_s.clock_end: No standing water remains above the bed and drainage has diminished to occasional drips; time is a reference, not a forced stop

recipe.completion_signal: No standing water above the coffee bed and flow diminished to occasional drips.

steps.instruction: Fold and fit #4 paper, rinse with hot water and discard rinse water. Move Clever off the server onto a level non-actuating surface; tare scale.
steps.why: Seats the filter, warms equipment and closes the bottom valve for immersion.
steps.completion: Paper sits neatly and rinse water has been discarded; brewer is off the server.

steps.instruction: Add all 400 g freshly boiled water before the coffee, leaving space below the rim.
steps.why: Preserves the selected water-first procedure and measured input.
steps.completion: Scale reads 400 g and water is retained.

steps.instruction: Add 25 g coffee, start timer at first coffee-water contact and stir gently until dry pockets disappear.
steps.why: Makes extraction time reproducible and wets the grounds.
steps.completion: All coffee is wet, with no dry pockets.

steps.instruction: Leave the mixture until the timer reaches 120 seconds, counting initial mixing within this interval.
steps.why: Allows the selected immersion period before disturbing the surface crust.
steps.completion: Timer reaches 120 seconds.

steps.instruction: At 120 seconds gently stir the surface crust back in, then leave it to settle for 30 seconds.
steps.why: Keeps the published crust-breaking and settling sequence intact.
steps.completion: Timer reaches 150 seconds after gentle stirring and settlement.

steps.instruction: At 150 seconds place Clever securely on a compatible server. Expect 45-75 seconds drainage, but observe completion rather than forcibly stopping at the reference time.
steps.why: The server opens the valve and paper separates the grounds from the drink.
steps.completion: No standing water above bed and flow has diminished to occasional drips.

steps.instruction: Lift by the handle onto the coaster after drainage, allow the beverage to cool and taste.
steps.why: Stops the valve being actuated and allows a safer, clearer taste assessment.
steps.completion: Brewer is stable off the server and the drink is comfortable to taste.

safety: Use a stable heat-safe server that supports the brewer and has room for the entire batch; test actuator fit with cold water first.
Keep below the rim with room for coffee; the 400 g recipe requires a large brewer.
Lift by the handle; avoid hot liquid and do not manually depress the outlet from beneath a filled brewer.
Let brewer cool, discard grounds and paper, then clean according to the model's instructions and check valve residue before reuse.
Dishwasher compatibility and seal disassembly were not verified; no universal instructions for either are asserted.

steps.completion: Smooth low-pressure descent ends at the grounds; otherwise stop and follow the maker's recovery instructions.

steps.completion: Coffee has been safely transferred; cool the equipment before cleaning.

Keep the removable stainless-steel ball from being lost during washing. Wear gloves when detaching or attaching the glass and base, follow the assembly diagram, reseat securely and confirm lever movement before reuse.

steps.instruction: Inspect cold pot's gasket, filter plate, funnel and valve for correct placement, cleanliness and damage. Complete the supplied first-use procedure when new; never heat dry.

steps.instruction: Tighten metal sections securely while cold, without excessive force or levering by handle; close lid and orient safety valve away from yourself and others.
steps.why: Correct closure controls leaks; closed lid and valve orientation follow this model's manual and keep a possible steam jet away from people.
steps.completion: Securely assembled pot with closed lid and unobstructed valve directed away from people.

steps.instruction: Place pot stably on compatible active hob; start optional observation clock now. Use controlled low-to-medium heat, with gas flame confined beneath base and handle clear. Stay nearby.
steps.why: Controlled heating avoids forcing rapid delivery and overheating the finished coffee.
steps.completion: Coffee delivery begins; no joint leakage or abnormal valve discharge.

steps.instruction: Remove from heat at the first gurgling change, using handle and heat protection. Keep clear of steam and let remaining discharge settle on a heatproof trivet.
steps.why: This app-authored endpoint follows illy's cue rather than a generic timer or the goal of emptying the reservoir.
steps.completion: Heat removed; active discharge settles. A small boiler residue may remain.

steps.instruction: Once discharge settles, lift lid by knob from a safe position, stir and pour carefully. Allow complete cooling before unscrewing. Rinse aluminum parts with warm water without detergent or abrasives; dry fully and store unclosed.
steps.why: Stirring mixes collected coffee; full cooldown protects against hot metal, liquid and pressure, and compatible care protects aluminum.
steps.completion: Coffee served; completely cool, clean, dry pot ready for storage.

safety: Never heat the pot without water. A manufacturer-prescribed water-filled commissioning/descaling cycle is different from an empty dry run.
Fill below safety valve's lower edge; never cover, block or bypass it. Keep fitted valve maintained according to exact model instructions.
Use moka-specific grounds and a full loose basket; never tamp. Check gasket, filter plate and funnel before heating.
Assemble securely before heat and never use handle as tightening lever. Keep Moka Express lid closed during use and orient safety valve away from yourself and others.
Use compatible stable hob with controlled heat; keep gas flame inside base and handle clear. Stay nearby and keep children away.
If leakage or abnormal valve venting occurs, stop heat and allow cooling; never open hot or force a blockage with extra heat.
Keep face/hands clear of steam and hot coffee. Handle with heat protection and place on heatproof surface.
Wait for complete cooling and settled pressure before unscrewing or cleaning.
For classic aluminum Moka Express, hand wash with warm water without detergent/abrasives; no dishwasher. Do not automatically apply a roaster's coffee-cleaner suggestion to aluminum.
Stainless steel does not establish detergent/dishwasher compatibility; follow exact model/manual edition. Dry fully and store unclosed.

equipment: Presto 02822 6-cup electric percolator with matching cord, perk tube/washer, basket, basket lid and cover

expected_time_s.clock_end: Ready signal light illuminates; this indicates readiness rather than a power-off

steps.instruction: With the appliance cool and unplugged, prepare clean, matching parts. Before first use wash and rinse its interior, cover and basket assembly, keeping base and plug socket dry. Check that the perk-tube washer is clean and moves freely.
steps.why: Clean correctly fitted parts enable perking and keep the electrical connection dry.
steps.completion: Clean cool parts, freely moving washer, dry electrical base and socket

steps.instruction: Remove the assembly and fill fresh cold water to the internal four mark. Do not substitute four household cups or assume exactly twenty fluid ounces input water.
steps.why: This model uses reservoir marks; starting a warm consecutive pot can weaken brewing.
steps.completion: Cold water reaches the internal four mark, within the model's two-to-six range

steps.instruction: Place wraparound paper's central hole over the basket stem. Block the stem opening with a finger while adding four level measuring tablespoons of coarse coffee. Fold paper over the coffee and tuck excess inside the basket.
steps.why: A fitted filter and clear stem reduce grounds in the pot; the measured dose is repeatable without claiming its mass.
steps.completion: Coffee stays in the paper-lined basket and the stem opening remains clear

steps.instruction: Cover the basket with its metal lid. Seat the perk tube in the bottom perk well; hold it there while fitting the filled basket. Push the pot cover firmly into place.
steps.why: Mis-seated tubing or a stuck washer can stop circulation; a secured cover protects against scalding.
steps.completion: Tube seated, basket lid fitted and pot cover firmly secured

steps.instruction: Attach the cord to the filled closed appliance first, then a suitable 120 V AC wall outlet. Leave the lid closed and wait for its ready light.
steps.why: The electric model manages brewing; an elapsed timer or stovetop perking window cannot replace its ready indicator.
steps.completion: Ready signal light illuminates

steps.instruction: Disconnect the wall plug first, then the appliance cord before lifting the pot. Pour using its handle with the cover secured. Optional keep-warm operates while stationary and plugged in; for later service transfer coffee to a thermal carafe.
steps.why: Ready does not mean power-off. Disconnecting before lifting simplifies cord handling; serving promptly limits prolonged hot holding.
steps.completion: Coffee served or transferred and appliance disconnected

steps.instruction: Let the unplugged appliance cool before removing parts and grounds. Wash and rinse interior, cover and basket assembly without wetting base or plug socket. Only the tube, basket and basket lid are expressly dishwasher-compatible. Dry before reuse.
steps.why: Cooling prevents burns; keeping electrical parts dry prevents shock and damage.
steps.completion: Clean freely moving washer and fully dry base/socket; grounds and filter discarded

Never plug in the Presto without water or liquid coffee. Use matching manufacturer-recommended parts; do not energize damaged equipment.
Keep the lid secured during brewing and serving. Do not remove it while brewing; coffee, grounds and metal parts can scald. Use the handle.
Attach cord to appliance before wall outlet; disconnect wall outlet then appliance before lifting to serve. Keep-warm operates while stationary and plugged in; ready light does not mean power-off.
Unplug and allow cooling before dismantling or cleaning. Do not immerse electric appliance, cord or plugs, or wet base or plug receptacle. Dry fully before reuse.

steps.why: Separate brewer removal from optional dilution, condensed milk or ice.
steps.completion: Phin is supported safely and coffee is ready for the chosen serving.

recipe.name: Jonathan Gagne steeped bloom, 20 g / 340 g paper example
equipment: Full-size NextLevel Pulsar with base, barrel and dispersion cap
Stable heat-safe server that supports the brewer level and holds the collected brew
recipe.grind_description: Relatively coarse and even, a little coarser than a typical 20 g V60 grind; tune on this brewer without inferring a grinder dial value or precise micron conversion.

expected_time_s.clock_start: Start the timer as the first 60 g bloom pour begins
expected_time_s.clock_end: Final drawdown: standing water has gone and flow has subsided to final drips

recipe.completion_signal: No standing water above the coffee bed and the final drawdown has subsided; close the valve and lift only by the base. The time range is a comparison target, not forced completion.

steps.instruction: With the barrel off, close the valve, add a shallow water layer just above the ridges, place dry paper on it, open over the sink, and close again. Fit the barrel firmly, threaded end downward.
steps.why: Seat the filter with minimal trapped air. This rinse is discarded and excluded from the brew input.
steps.completion: Paper flat on ridges; barrel firmly seated with no leak. Valve closed.

steps.instruction: Place level on a stable server and scale, add 20 g coffee, level gently without tamping, fit the cap and tare. Stabilize the base while operating the valve: horizontal is closed, upright is open.
steps.why: A level coffee bed and supported brewer allow even wetting and safe valve operation.
steps.completion: Level coffee bed, cap fitted and scale reads zero.

steps.instruction: Open the valve, start the timer and pour 60 g through the dispersion cap. Close as soon as dripping begins, even during the pour, and finish reaching 60 g. Holding only the base, swirl gently to wet dry pockets.
steps.why: The brief open start displaces air between coffee particles; closing then retains the bloom. Avoid driving fines into the paper with strong agitation.
steps.completion: Scale at 60 g, grounds wet, valve closed and bloom retained.

steps.instruction: Keep the valve closed until elapsed time reaches 60 seconds from the beginning of the first pour.
steps.why: Allow saturation before draining resumes; 60 seconds is an elapsed release point, not an extra wait after pouring.
steps.completion: Elapsed timer reads 60 seconds; retained bloom remains wet.

steps.instruction: At elapsed 60 seconds open the valve fully. Add 280 g through the cap in small pulses, keeping about 1 cm of water over the bed; stop at 340 g cumulative. With a gooseneck kettle, Gagne recommends relatively fast circular pouring to avoid digging holes; ordinary kettles also work. No fixed pulse count, size or universal pouring rate is specified.
steps.why: The low pool supports ongoing percolation while limiting unnecessarily tall water levels. The total already includes the 60 g bloom.
steps.completion: 340 g cumulative brew water has entered; level safely below rim.

steps.instruction: Let final drawdown finish with the valve open. Once standing water is gone and flow subsides, close, lift only by the base, set down safely, and serve.
steps.why: Slowing as the water level drops is normal; drainage rather than a timer deadline determines removal.
steps.completion: Final drawdown complete; brewer safely removed by the base.

safety: Lift the assembled brewer only by its base whenever it contains hot brew water; never lift it by the barrel walls.
Support the brewer and server level and stabilize the base during valve operation. Stop pouring before approaching the rim; ensure server capacity is sufficient.
Chamber liquid volume is 380 mL; coffee displaces space. It is not a 380 g cumulative-water limit or permission to retain 340 g plus coffee without checking level.

Keep brewer parts off hot surfaces, inspect for damage and wash before first use. Hand washing is encouraged; dishwasher use is allowed but detergent residues can affect taste. Avoid chlorine or bleach.

After cooling, dispose of paper/grounds, rinse and wipe oils from the barrel; store with barrel removed. Metal discs require the separate manufacturer cleanup, washing and protective storage procedure.

equipment: Hario Technica TCAR-3, practical capacity 360 mL, supplied mounted stand and upper-bowl support

steps.instruction: Inspect intact glass and gasket, secure the lower bowl fastener, rinse the brewer and work on a level dry heat-safe surface. Dip new cloth in boiling water, center its assembly and pull the chain down to hook it at the upper stem end.
steps.why: A secure mount, seal and filter are prerequisites for controlled transfer and filtration.
steps.completion: Stand is secure, glass is undamaged and cloth assembly is centered and hooked.

steps.instruction: Add 30 g medium-ground coffee to the upper chamber above the cloth. Keep the chamber in its support.
steps.why: This baseline follows Hario's coffee-first sequence, rather than a water-first roaster recipe.
steps.completion: All measured coffee is in the upper chamber before heating and transfer.

steps.instruction: Add 360 mL water to the lower bowl, up to its three-cup mark; dry the outside. Hot water may shorten heating, but no exact initial temperature is required here.
steps.why: Hario defines each marked water cup as 120 mL. Brimful capacity is not a brew target.
steps.completion: Lower bowl is filled to the three-cup mark and its outside is dry.

steps.instruction: While the lamp is unlit, set approximately 3 mm exposed wick. Center it under the bowl, then light it and keep the flame below 4 cm. Rest the upper chamber at an angle; when water starts boiling, seat it gently upright. Watch water rise, with a little remaining below.
steps.why: Heating and water transfer precede the timed post-transfer steep; early upright sealing changes the procedure.
steps.completion: Water has risen into the upper chamber; heating and transfer have no universal deadline.

steps.instruction: After completed transfer, stir gently to wet and loosen grounds. Start our steep clock immediately when this initial stir ends. Continue controlled centered heating for the selected 60 seconds; avoid overheating the nearly empty lower bowl.
steps.why: 60 seconds is our selected point within Hario's 40-60-second range. The manual gives water-rise, stir and heat sequence without explicit stopwatch zero; starting immediately after the initial stir is our editorial convention, not an exact published mandatory prescription.
steps.completion: The selected 60-second clock from the end of the initial gentle stir has elapsed; coffee is fully wetted.

steps.instruction: At the selected 60-second steep endpoint, use dry heat protection to move the mounted stand away from the stationary lamp, then snuff the lamp with its cover and check that it is out. Never move a lit lamp.
steps.why: Removing heat lets the lower chamber cool and initiates filtered return.
steps.completion: Brewer is clear of the heat source and the lamp flame is completely extinguished.

steps.instruction: Let the coffee return naturally through the cloth. Record this as a separate return duration. Wait for liquid flow to stop; do not force the hot chambers apart.
steps.why: Return is observed rather than ended by an invented deadline.
steps.completion: Coffee has returned to the lower bowl and liquid flow has stopped.

steps.instruction: Hold the stand securely, gently rock the upper chamber free and place it in its support. Serve with dry heat protection as needed.
steps.why: Waiting for return completion avoids pulling apart an active hot assembly.
steps.completion: Upper chamber rests securely in its support and coffee is served safely.

steps.instruction: Cool glass before washing it with mild detergent and a nonabrasive sponge. Wash and gently brush cloth, then store submerged in fresh water in the refrigerator, changing water regularly.
steps.why: Glass care and cloth care are distinct; hot glass and wet contact risk thermal shock.
steps.completion: Cooled brewer is clean and cloth has been cleaned and stored correctly.

safety: Inspect glass and gasket, secure the lower bowl fastener and use a stable dry heat-safe surface away from combustibles and children. Use only the matching siphon heat source.
Dry the outside before heating. Never heat dry glass or continue unnecessary heating when the lower bowl is nearly empty. Keep hands and face clear of possible hot-water spurts.

For the supplied Hario alcohol lamp only: use liquid fuel-type alcohol; not gel fuel, gasoline, benzene or kerosene. Fill no higher than its holder level. Use the supplied wick, about 3 mm exposed, and flame under 4 cm. Prepare and adjust while unlit.
Do not move or refill a lit lamp. Snuff with its cover and verify extinction. Read the actual fuel-container instructions; this guide has not verified a particular formulation or ventilation label.

The stand and glass can be hot. Use dry heat protection when moving the mounted stand. Wait for complete return before gently separating the upper chamber; do not force, yank or strongly twist hot glass.

Prevent thermal shock: let glass cool before washing, touching it with a wet cloth or placing it on a wet surface. Do not strike glass with a metal implement; use mild detergent and nonabrasive cleaning after cooling.

Cloth is cleaned and stored submerged in fresh water in the refrigerator with regular water changes. Paper is disposable; the separate NXA/SCA metal assembly is washed and dried. Do not apply one material's preparation or storage to another.

variants.name: Hario older intermediate guide
variants.how_it_differs: 15 g/250 g, 92–96 °C, about 30-second bloom of unspecified mass, then continuous circular pour; 2.5-minute wording lacks explicit clock origin.

variants.name: Rao Hario interview recipe
variants.how_it_differs: 20 g in plastic V60, 97 °C, source 60/200/330 mL cumulative targets; aggressive bloom spin and brief gentle settling spins. Final pour follows about 70 percent drainage; typical total 240–270 seconds.

variants.name: Kasuya interview 4:6
variants.how_it_differs: 20 g coarse coffee, 300 mL at 92 °C; five source additions 50/70/60/60/60 mL at 0/45/90/130/160 seconds; removal at 210. Identify conventional versus modified ceramic geometry before implementation.

variants.name: Kurasu flash iced
variants.how_it_differs: 16 g, 150 g hot water at 91 °C plus 70 g brew ice; hot additions 40/60/50 g at 0/40/70 seconds, about ten seconds each. Approximate drawdown 130 seconds; melt brew ice before serving. Hot input ratio 1:9.375, hot water plus ice 1:13.75; neither is beverage yield.

variants.name: Other sizes, materials or paper
variants.how_it_differs: Use matching filter size and revalidate dose, pour behavior and drainage; cup labels are not universal volume capacities.

troubleshooting.check_first: Check matching seated paper, unobstructed outlet, receiver airflow and recent paper changes.
troubleshooting.adjustment: If still slow and harsh, grind slightly coarser; repeat consistent pouring.

troubleshooting.check_first: Confirm zero, dose, level bed and that water reaches grounds rather than paper edge.
troubleshooting.adjustment: Try slightly finer grind; change one variable before tasting again.

troubleshooting.check_first: Confirm recipe and equipment before diagnosing from elapsed time.
troubleshooting.adjustment: Try slightly coarser grind; maintain other inputs.
